answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation-weighted payments. A beacon of useful work builds trust slowly, while proven fraud burns the stake and can forfeit pending rewards; splitting into many identities does not multiply influence unless the attacker also locks proportionally more capital. The zenith of the defense is not perfect identity proof, but making each fake account costly to fund and risky to operate, with honest newcomers able to climb the same ledge through sustained work.
